A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ArticulatedGS work, with readable text, equations, figures, and tables. The main sections align closely. v1 includes supplementary Sections 6–7; the supplied v2 ends after the references, despite retaining references to supplementary material. This is an observable omission, not an extraction failure.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, motion-estimation, and novel-view results in Tables 1–2, plus supplementary ablations and qualitative failure cases.

after.justification: v2 retains the original ArticulatedGS results in Tables 1–2 and the main qualitative evaluations, although the supplementary results are absent.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.6 retain the same staged optimization, DeformNet architecture, appearance/ARAP/geometric losses, mask thresholds, and sequential multi-part procedure. The omitted implementation details do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The main PARIS synthetic/real benchmark and custom-object demonstrations remain. Additional custom categories shown in v1 Figure 10, including lighter and door examples, and the basket/window cases in Figure 15 are absent from v2, narrowing the reported object and difficult-case coverage.

E2.justification: v1 Table 3 compares ArticulatedGS with published Artnerf results; this comparison is absent in v2. Artnerf is renamed DTA in the discussion but remains the same cited work [41]. Ditto, PARIS, Vanilla, and DGS comparisons remain; newly cited LEIA, ArtGS, and Deng work are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: No setting for a retained experiment is substantively revised: the pretrained-Ditto comparison, Vanilla setup, and main evaluation remain unchanged. The disappearance of supplementary view splits, sampling instructions, and training budgets reduces documentation rather than reporting replacement settings.

E4.justification: v2 retains the Vanilla ablation in Section 4.3 but omits the ARAP, geometric-loss, and loss-balancing ablations in v1 Table 4, the threshold sensitivity test in Figure 14, depth inspection in Figure 13, and failure cases in Figure 15. This substantially reduces component validation and diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 in both versions states that results are summarized over 10 trials. Neither provides seed specifications, dispersion estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the omitted supplement introduces no separate uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 are numerically identical. v2 omits the Artnerf-specific rows from Table 3, the loss-ablation results from Table 4, and distinct supplementary qualitative findings. For example, the start-state PSNR comparison of 39.83 for the full method versus 37.62 without geometric loss disappears. Figure 6 also corrects the Ours/DGS attribution for the stapler sequence.

T1.justification: The Gaussian and joint representations, assumptions, optimization formulation, and Equations 1–10 are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes a theorem or proof; the omitted standard evaluation-metric descriptions do not constitute a theoretical revision.

C1.justification: v2 changes the contribution from 'The first 3D Gaussian model' to 'A 3D Gaussian model' and removes the related-work statement claiming the first such method for human-made articulated objects. Claims about self-supervision, staged optimization, accuracy, and efficiency remain.

C2.justification: v2 retains the main alignment, lighting, and annotation caveats but loses Section 7's explanations of small-part and similar-appearance failures. It also omits qualifications about symmetry/occlusion, situations where added losses help little, and Artnerf's depth/noise advantage. These omissions substantially narrow the discussion of mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v1 Section 6 specifies PyTorch/RTX3090, 5,000/10,000/3,000/10,000 optimization steps, 9–12-minute runtime, 100 training/50 test views per state, 10,000-point sampling, and LPIPS(VGG). These details are absent in v2. Its abstract adds a project-website pointer and a future code-release promise, which does not establish code availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds LEIA, Deng's Articulate Your NeRF, and ArtGS and withdraws the explicit priority claim. DrivingGaussian and the appendix-associated Blender, Instant-NGP, and PyTorch references disappear. This is a targeted positioning update; Artnerf-to-DTA is a rename, not a newly cited work.

P1.justification: The main Sections 1–5 retain their order and largely identical prose. Editing is localized to the website sentence, novelty wording, related-work terminology, and shortened captions. The supplementary sections are omitted rather than rewritten or integrated into the main narrative.

P2.justification: Supplementary Tables 3–4 and Figures 9–15 disappear, removing substantial displays beyond the examples retained in the main text. Retained raster images have higher resolution. Figure 6 corrects the stapler Ours/DGS labels, while Figure 2 loses several mathematical annotations; some captions are shortened and text reflows.

improvement.justification: v2 improves image sharpness, corrects Figure 6 labels, and moderates novelty positioning. However, omitting the supplementary implementation and evaluation details, component ablations, Artnerf comparison, and concrete failure analysis substantially weakens reproducibility and support for the method's design and applicability. The main results remain unchanged, and references to the absent supplement persist. These losses outweigh the presentation and positioning gains.
